title: The ethics of making up data

cues.en: Presenter: I'd like to take a few moments to discuss the ethics of making up data or faking data.
cues.zh: 我想花一點時間，討論編造資料或偽造資料的倫理。

cues.en: Now, you probably think that this doesn't need an entire video because you might think the answer is simple, that it's unethical to make up data, but actually it's a little bit more nuanced than that
cues.zh: 你可能覺得不需要一整部影片，因為答案很簡單：編造資料不道德。但其實事情稍微更有層次，

cues.en: as I will shortly explain.
cues.zh: 我馬上就會說明。

cues.en: So first of all, faking data and presenting it as if it were real data, so making up or manipulating your data, is really bad and you definitely shouldn't do it.
cues.zh: 首先，偽造資料並當作真實資料呈現，也就是編造或操弄資料，真的很糟，絕對不應該做。

cues.en: You might lose your job, or even if you don't lose your job, you might lose your reputation.
cues.zh: 可能失去工作，即使沒失去工作，也可能失去聲譽。

cues.en: And if you're working with other people on a project, so your collaborators or team members or people in your department, they might lose their jobs or their reputations
cues.zh: 如果與其他人合作專案，例如合作者、團隊成員，或部門同仁，他們也可能失去工作或聲譽，

cues.en: because of something you did when faking data.
cues.zh: 就因為你偽造資料時做的事。

cues.en: And if the data that you are working with are, let's say, some safety data in a manufacturing plant or something like that, then faking or manipulating your data
cues.zh: 如果處理的，例如是製造工廠的安全資料，偽造或操弄，

cues.en: can literally put other people in physical harm, possibly costing their lives.
cues.zh: 真的可能使其他人受到身體傷害，甚至失去生命。

cues.en: So this is really bad.
cues.zh: 所以這真的很糟。

cues.en: You don't wanna do any of these things.
cues.zh: 這些事，你都不會想做。

cues.en: So therefore, you shouldn't fake your data.
cues.zh: 因此，不應該偽造資料。

cues.en: You shouldn't make up your data.
cues.zh: 不應該編造資料。

cues.en: But let me be clear that that doesn't mean that you can't make mistakes.
cues.zh: 但要釐清，這不代表不能犯錯。

cues.en: Everyone makes mistakes.
cues.zh: 每個人都會犯錯。

cues.en: People make mistakes with coding, with data.
cues.zh: 程式碼、資料，都可能出錯。

cues.en: Making mistakes is just a natural part of being human.
cues.zh: 犯錯是人之常情。

cues.en: The difference is that honest mistakes are unintentional.
cues.zh: 差別是，無心之失並非故意。

cues.en: So these are just little bugs in your code or you know, you press the wrong button in your statistics analysis package or something like that.
cues.zh: 例如程式碼的小錯誤，或在統計分析軟體裡按錯按鈕等。

cues.en: So when you make an honest mistake, then you admit to it, you apologize, you correct the mistake, and you move on, and it's totally fine.
cues.zh: 無心犯錯時，就承認、道歉、修正錯誤，再繼續，完全沒問題。

cues.en: An honest mistake should not cost you your job or your reputation.
cues.zh: 無心之失不應該讓你失去工作或聲譽。

cues.en: Maybe a little different if you're making mistakes all the time, but everyone makes mistakes now and then.
cues.zh: 如果一直犯錯，也許另當別論，但每個人偶爾都會犯錯。

cues.en: I've certainly made mistakes, and when I catch them or when other people notice them, then I do this.
cues.zh: 我當然也犯過錯，自己發現，或其他人注意到時，就這樣做。

cues.en: I admit that it's a mistake, I apologize, I fix it, and I move on.
cues.zh: 承認是錯誤，道歉、修正，再繼續。

cues.en: There might even be mistakes in this course.
cues.zh: 這門課甚至可能也有錯誤。

cues.en: They're all unintentional, of course, but you know, it happens that there's a little typo in an equation or something is a little bit wrong with the code.
cues.zh: 當然都不是故意的，但方程式有小筆誤，或程式碼稍有問題，就是可能發生。

cues.en: So you will see probably within a year of publishing this course, there will probably be more than one.
cues.zh: 所以大概在課程發布後一年內，你可能會看到，不只一個。

cues.en: I'm guessing. I don't hope.
cues.zh: 這是猜測，不是希望如此。

cues.en: But I guess there will be at least a few points in this course that I have to correct because I made an honest mistake.
cues.zh: 但我猜，課程至少會有幾個地方，需要因為無心之失而修正。

cues.en: But that is quite different from intentionally manipulating or faking your data.
cues.zh: 這和刻意操弄或偽造資料，非常不同。

cues.en: You can see the key difference is whether it's unintentional or intentional.
cues.zh: 關鍵差別，就在於無心，還是故意。

cues.en: So just don't do it.
cues.zh: 所以就是不要做。

cues.en: Really, it's that simple when it comes to manipulating or faking data that you present as real data.
cues.zh: 對於操弄、偽造資料，卻當成真實資料呈現這件事，真的就這麼簡單。

cues.en: On the other hand, making up data can actually be a really powerful way to learn about statistics and data analysis methods.
cues.zh: 另一方面，編造資料，其實能非常有效地學習統計與資料分析方法。

cues.en: So in fact, well, when you're doing it on purpose and it's for good, then usually we call that simulating data instead of fabricating data.
cues.zh: 當你有意這麼做，而且用意良好時，通常叫做模擬資料，而不是捏造資料。

cues.en: There's quite a few reasons why simulating data is really awesome, including it allows you to validate your statistical analysis methods.
cues.zh: 模擬資料很棒，有很多理由，包括可以驗證統計分析方法。

cues.en: This is particularly important if you are developing new statistical methods or extending different methods in unique ways.
cues.zh: 開發新統計方法，或以獨特方式延伸不同方法時，這特別重要。

cues.en: It allows you to learn the advantages and the limitations of different analysis methods.
cues.zh: 它讓你了解不同分析方法的優點與限制。

cues.en: And I use this quite often in the course.
cues.zh: 我在課程中經常使用。

cues.en: For example, seeing how your statistical method, let's say a T-test, is affected by the sample size and the signal size and the noise.
cues.zh: 例如，觀察樣本數、訊號大小與雜訊，如何影響統計方法，例如 t 檢定。

cues.en: So faking your data allows you to control the size of the effects, the amount of noise, the characteristics of the noise, the sample size, and so on.
cues.zh: 所以，編造資料讓你控制效應大小、雜訊量、雜訊特性、樣本數等等。

cues.en: These sorts of things are not possible to control in real data.
cues.zh: 真實資料裡，這些東西無法控制。

cues.en: You just get the data that you get.
cues.zh: 得到什麼資料，就是什麼資料。

cues.en: So when you simulate data, you can control all sorts of features of the data.
cues.zh: 所以模擬資料時，能控制資料的各種特徵。

cues.en: So that also allows you to understand your data better because it forces you to think carefully and critically about how data are constructed,
cues.zh: 這也能幫助你更了解資料，因為迫使你仔細、批判地思考，資料如何建構，

cues.en: how signals are mixed with noise, how different groups interact with each other, and so on.
cues.zh: 訊號如何與雜訊混合，不同群體如何互動等等。

cues.en: So therefore, I think simulating data also improves your thinking skills and improves your coding skills.
cues.zh: 因此，我認為模擬資料也能改善思考與程式能力。

cues.en: And I admit that I'm a little bit nerdy.
cues.zh: 我承認自己有點宅。

cues.en: I have some nerdy tendencies now and then, but I think it's also kind of fun to simulate data.
cues.zh: 偶爾有些宅的傾向，但我也覺得模擬資料有點好玩。

cues.en: So what is the deal?
cues.zh: 所以到底怎麼回事？

cues.en: Is faking your data really horrible and could lose you your job?
cues.zh: 偽造資料是非常糟，可能讓你失去工作？

cues.en: Or is it really awesome and will help you learn?
cues.zh: 還是非常棒，能幫助學習？

cues.en: Well, the answer is both.
cues.zh: 答案是兩者都是。

cues.en: It really depends on the presentation.
cues.zh: 真正取決於呈現方式。

cues.en: So the unethical parts of making up data is when you fake your data and you tell other people that it's real, or you mislead other people into thinking that it's real.
cues.zh: 編造資料不道德的部分，是偽造後告訴別人是真的，或誤導別人以為是真的。

cues.en: That is bad.
cues.zh: 那不好。

cues.en: That is unethical.
cues.zh: 那不道德。

cues.en: On the other hand, when you tell your audience beforehand that the data are made up, they're simulated, they're fabricated, whatever terms you want to use, that's totally fine, and it can be really advantageous.
cues.zh: 另一方面，事先告訴觀眾，資料是編造、模擬、捏造，不論你想用哪個詞，都完全沒問題，而且可能非常有益。

cues.en: You just explain why you made up the data, and then it's fine.
cues.zh: 只要說明為什麼編造資料，就沒問題。

cues.en: Then there's no uncertainty or ambiguity.
cues.zh: 就沒有不確定或歧義。

cues.en: Okay, so in the interest of doing what I'm telling you that you should do, I'm now going to tell you that all of the data that you will see in this course are made up.
cues.zh: 為了以身作則，實踐我告訴你該做的事，現在我要告訴你，這門課看到的所有資料，都是編造的。

cues.en: It's all fake data.
cues.zh: 全部都是假資料。

cues.en: I faked, I fabricated all the data in this course, and I did this for a good reason.
cues.zh: 我偽造、編造了本課程所有資料，而且有充分理由。

cues.en: I really believe that using fabricated data or simulated data is the best way to learn statistics.
cues.zh: 我真的相信，使用編造或模擬資料，是學統計最好的方式。

cues.en: It's the best way to gain intuition about various statistical analyses because there are all sorts of features of the data that we cannot control in real data.
cues.zh: 這是建立各種統計分析直覺的最佳方式，因為真實資料的各種特徵，我們無法控制。

cues.en: We cannot know the ground truth in real data, but we can know the real truth, we can know the underlying true dynamics of simulated data,
cues.zh: 真實資料中，我們無法知道真實情況，但模擬資料中，可以知道真正情況、底層的真實動態，

cues.en: and we can control various features of the data.
cues.zh: 也能控制資料的各種特徵。

cues.en: And that allows us to explore these data analysis methods in ways that is not possible when only using real data.
cues.zh: 因此可以用只靠真實資料無法做到的方式，探索這些資料分析方法。

cues.en: So I think all statistics courses should have made up data and not real data.
cues.zh: 所以我認為，所有統計課都應該用編造資料，而非真實資料。

cues.en: That's just my opinion.
cues.zh: 這只是我的看法。

cues.en: Nonetheless, I hope you see that there's a clear distinction between the ethics of making up data.
cues.zh: 總之，希望你能看到，編造資料的倫理，有清楚區別。

cues.en: And essentially it's bad when you tell other people that it is real data and it's good when you tell people that it is fake data so they know
cues.zh: 基本上，告訴別人它是真資料，就不好；告訴別人它是假資料，讓大家知道，

cues.en: and you're using it for some kind of education or exploratory experience.
cues.zh: 並用於教育或探索性的經驗，就很好。
